input.explanation:
Fault: the scrape target is selected by port *name*, and the two halves of that contract live in two files nothing reconciles. The 10:15:00Z deploy renamed the port in deploy/values-production.yaml (portName: metrics -> http-metrics) for the estate-wide `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, but deploy/scrape.yaml still selects `port: metrics`. A ServiceMonitor endpoint naming a port no Service exposes is not an error to the operator - it is an empty target list - so the shop kept serving /metrics and rendering account pages normally while the series stopped at exactly the deploy minute. That is the signature in the incident: onset at the deploy, no failing requests, no samples.

Fix: scrape.yaml now selects `port: http-metrics`, so the renamed port is scraped again and the convention-conforming deploy is safe to take. A new test, tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py, reads both deploy files and asserts the name the ServiceMonitor selects is the name metrics.portName gives the port. Against the code as it stands (`metrics` vs `http-metrics`) that assertion fails; with this change it passes, and it fails again the next time either side is renamed alone - the only durable guard, since nothing in the cluster reports this mismatch. It also pins the scrape interval at no slower than the one-minute no-sample alert expects.

The test scans the two documents line by line rather than importing PyYAML, so it adds no dependency. Nothing in src/ reads either file, so no service code needed changing.

files.content:
# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# A stand-in for io-shop's manifest, not a real one: no cluster applies this
# file, and nothing in this repository reads it. It is written as the
# ServiceMonitor such a cluster would carry, so that how the shop is collected
# is in the repository beside how it is deployed. Its labels are illustrative.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. A name that matches no port is not an error to the operator,
# it is a target list with nothing in it, and the shop goes on serving metrics
# nobody collects - so tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py reads both files and
# fails if the two names drift apart.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s

input.summary: Point the ServiceMonitor at the renamed `http-metrics` port and test that scrape config and values agree
